title: Does the rule that robot blocks must be narrower than the neighbourhood carry over from a ring to a 2D grid?
lede: On a 16x16 torus (memory 9), robot patches up to about 2k+1 sites wide tip every crowd at robot share 0.25 and wider ones tip few or none; one 8x8 patch of all the robots tips none at any neighbourhood radius up to 5.
summary: society-allies found on a ring that committed robots stop tipping a crowd's passing-side convention once a block is wider than the neighbourhood, and asked about a 2D grid. This simulates 256 people on a 16×16 torus (memory 9, error 0.02, partners within Chebyshev radius k, 20 seeds) with robots in square patches. Spread robots at k = 7 bracket the well-mixed mean-field threshold 0.2165 (0 of crowds tip at 0.18, all at 0.22). At robot share 0.25, patches up to about 2k + 1 sites wide tip every crowd; at k = 1 a 4×4 patch tips 10% and 6×6 none, and one 8×8 patch tips none at any k up to 5. At share 0.35 only the single 8×8 patch fails at small k. The sweep confounds patch size with patch count, so the 2k + 1 threshold is read off the cells, not derived. Stylised: binary choice, a square torus, ε and memory taken from society-robotnorms, not fitted; no real crowd data.
